claim: Test-based repair that passes the tests often overfits: of the 55 of 105 bugs GenProg was reported to fix, a re-examination (Qi et al. 2015) found a correct patch for only 2 of 105, and 104 of its 110 plausible patches were equivalent to a single functionality deletion. (Weimer et al. 2009's 59% is a per-trial search success rate on ten programs, a different measure.)
agent_test: Run our agent's repair loop with only visible tests vs with held-out tests at equal tokens; report plausible vs correct rate.
audit_note: Qi et al. 2015 numbers (2 of 105 correct; 104 of 110 plausible patches equal one deletion) verified, but the 59% in Weimer 2009 is the per-trial search success rate on ten programs, not GenProg's 'claim'; the claim Qi tests is 55 of 105 bugs fixed (a later study), and Weimer 2009 is not the system Qi analysed.
claim_before_audit: Test-based repair that passes the tests often overfits: GenProg's reported fixes were mostly not correct (2 of 105 correct; 104 of 110 plausible patches equal one deletion), against its own 59% success claim.

claim: Human debugging studies conflict on whether ranked fault lists help: Parnin and Orso found no overall speed gain (Tetris 12:42 vs 14:14, n.s.; N=34); Xia et al. found about 2x faster with an accurate tool (11.38 vs 26.45 min, 36 professionals).
agent_test: Give the agent a ranked suspect list of controlled accuracy (accurate, mediocre, none) at equal tokens; measure time-to-root-cause tokens.

claim: Tool accuracy moderates the benefit: mediocre list 16.35 min and 94% success, accurate list 11.38 min and 98%, none 26.45 min and 77%.
agent_test: Same three-arm test with degraded rankers; check if agent over-trusts bad lists.

claim: Users do not walk a ranked list in order and do not stop on meeting the fault: 37% of visits skip ahead, and people kept inspecting about 10 more minutes (61% of time) after clicking the faulty line.
agent_test: Log whether agent verifies a located fault or keeps wandering; add a stop-on-confirmed-cause rule and compare tokens.

claim: Evaluation on artificial faults is a weak proxy: Pearson et al. found rankings and significance on mutants (2995) differ from real faults (310); hybrid reaches top-5 36% best case, 23% average case.
agent_test: Evaluate our localiser on real and seeded bugs separately; require agreement.

claim: LLM localisation with test-failure context beats spectrum (Ochiai) on Java and Python: AutoFL +19.7% acc@1 (Defects4J), +166.7% (BugsInPy, GPT-3.5), +233.3% (GPT-4).
agent_test: Compare agent with and without function-call navigation and an Ochiai hint, equal tokens, Defects4J subset.

claim: Independent LLM-localisation systems report Top-1 gains over non-LLM baselines on Defects4J: LLMAO 22.3% vs Ochiai 4.8% (395 bugs, v1.2.0); ChatGPT-4 with error log 23.13 vs SmartFL 15.75 (function-level mean Acc@1); AgentFL 157 of 395 (v1.2.0, beating ChatGPT/LLMAO baselines, but FlexFL's reproduction got 144); FlexFL 164 vs Ochiai 122 on the 353-bug v1.0 subset used by AutoFL.
agent_test: Baseline: scaffold agent vs Ochiai on same bugs; report Top-1/3/5 at equal tokens.
audit_note: LLMAO 22.3 vs Ochiai 4.8, ChatGPT-4 23.13 vs SmartFL 15.75, AgentFL 157/395 and FlexFL 164 verified, but only LLMAO and FlexFL are compared against Ochiai (ChatGPT-4 is vs SmartFL, AgentFL vs LLM baselines), FlexFL's 164 vs 122 is on AutoFL's 353-bug Defects4J v1.0 subset (not 'v1.2'), and FlexFL's own re-run of AgentFL gave 144 not 157.
claim_before_audit: Independent LLM-localisation systems all beat Ochiai at Top-1: LLMAO 22.3% vs 4.8%; ChatGPT-4 w/ log 23.13 vs SmartFL 15.75; AgentFL 157/395; FlexFL 164 vs Ochiai 122 on a v1.2 subset.

claim: Giving the model the failing-test error log is the single most valuable context: removing it cut Top-1 by 25.6%; test-failure analysis removal cut AgentFL Top-1 by 20%. Prompt-level confirmation: in FuseFL, test results alone gave 187 Top-1 vs 169 for Ochiai scores alone (324 faults, GPT-3.5).
agent_test: Ablate error-log and stack trace in the agent's prompt at equal tokens.
audit_note: Wu 25.6% (error log removal), AgentFL Top-1 157 to 125 (-20.4%), FuseFL TestRes 187 vs SusScore 169 all verified; FuseFL set is 324 student programs (Refactory) with GPT-3.5, not Defects4J, and AgentFL 'test failure analysis' is an LLM analysis step rather than raw log; 'single most valuable' holds within each paper's ablation.

claim: Confidence of an LLM localiser is calibrated: Spearman 0.57 (Defects4J) and 0.52 (BugsInPy) with Precision@1 over 5 reruns; self-consistency across repeats is a usable signal. Counter-evidence: for code generation, repair and completion, raw model confidence is poorly calibrated (ECE 0.09 to 0.73; reflective confidence inconsistent), so localisation confidence should be gated by reruns or execution.
agent_test: Run agent 5 times, use agreement as confidence; check correlation with correctness and use it to trigger more search.

claim: Structured divide and conquer in localisation helps: hierarchical file-class-line (Agentless: file 81.7%, skeleton beats full file), LLM4FL without Division -23.24% Top-1, without CodeNav -16.51%.
agent_test: Compare flat vs hierarchical localisation prompt at equal tokens.
audit_note: Agentless file 81.7% combined, skeleton 58.33% vs complete file 53.67% edit-location, LLM4FL -23.24%/-16.51% Top-1 all verified; LocAgent and LLM4FL are independent of Agentless.

claim: Localisation accuracy predicts repair success but not perfectly: a 90% file-hit tool solved only 23.67%; unrealistic (oracle) localisation inflates repair; realistic SBFL localisation cut RepairAgent fixes 25% and raised cost 81%. Agent-level check: file-level hits track resolve rate, but given a hit, repair success differed (82.2% vs 69.6%), so localisation is necessary not sufficient.
agent_test: Run repair with oracle vs realistic localisation to measure the gap; budget tokens for localisation.
audit_note: Agentless (OpenCSG 90.0% file-level, 23.67% solved), RepairAgent (16 bugs, 25% drop, 81% cost) and Meng et al. (82.2% vs 69.6%) numbers verified; RepairAgent result is on a small Defects4J subset with no extra cycles.

claim: Self-generated reproduction tests help: Agentless produced a reproducing test for 213 of 300 issues, but only 94 validated against the true patch, so test quality is a bottleneck.
agent_test: Add reproduction-test generation and filter; measure resolution at equal tokens.

claim: Self-repair gains are small once sampling budget is matched, and are limited by feedback quality: 1.05x pass@20 baseline; human feedback 52.60% vs GPT-4 feedback 33.30% overall. CodeMonkeys finds serial iterations and parallel samples give similar coverage at equal cost after the first few iterations.
agent_test: Match tokens between best-of-N and repair loops; swap in stronger critic.

claim: Bug location knowledge is partly memorised in SWE-bench: file-path identification up to 76% on Verified vs 53% outside; 63.75% of SWE-agent+GPT-4 resolved patches suspicious; accuracy fell 12.47% to 3.97%. Defects4J itself: 80% of its repositories sit in TheStack; repair success on Defects4J fell 4.1 to 16.0 points after identifier-renaming and other meaning-preserving edits, but not significantly on post-cutoff GitBug-Java for Claude-3.7 and GPT-4o (repair with function given, not localisation).
agent_test: Test the agent only on post-cutoff or private bugs; report contamination-free numbers.
audit_note: Verified: 76% vs 53% (Liang), 12.47 to 3.97 and 32.67+31.08=63.75% (SWE-Bench+ sums solution leakage and weak tests, which is leakage/test weakness rather than memorisation per se), TheStack 80% membership (Ramos), Defects4J drops 4.1 to 15.98 (De Koning; table shows GPT-4o -4.01) and GitBug-Java p=0.819/0.667 for Claude-3.7/GPT-4o.

claim: Real industrial bugs are much harder than benchmarks: human-reported Google bugs 25.6% plausible, 17.9% valid; machine-reported 73% and 43%; for human-reported failures only 3.5% still edit the correct file. On SWE-bench Verified, solved-by-all issues scored 1.95x higher on solution-in-report quality than solved-by-none, versus 1.01x for reproduction examples.
agent_test: Include noisy-report bugs in evaluation; test an issue-clarification step.

claim: ChatRepair (ChatGPT conversation with failing-test feedback) fixes 162 of 337 Defects4J/QuixBugs-scale bugs at about $0.42 each, with no repair templates needed; separately, giving ChatGPT hints such as the expected output raised it from 19 to 31 of 40 QuixBugs bugs (Codex without hints: 21).
agent_test: Add failing test name, message and line to the repair prompt; equal tokens.
audit_note: The 19 to 31 of 40 lift is ChatGPT's (Codex solved 21 without hints), not Codex's; and no cited source compares template/patch context against conversation/feedback, so the 'helps less' comparison is not supported.
claim_before_audit: Template/patch context helps less than conversation and feedback: ChatGPT-conversation repair with failing-test info fixes 162/337 at $0.42; hints (expected output) lifted Codex from 19 to 31 of 40.

claim: More tool calls on failures: RepairAgent used 6 write-fix calls on fixed bugs vs 17 on unfixed; memory and state machine ablations raise cost and repeat commands. Independent support: failed trajectories are longer (RepairAgent 40 vs 22 iterations; OpenHands 54 rounds to cover 80% of failures vs 25 for successes).
agent_test: Cap repeat edits; trigger re-localisation after N failed patches.
audit_note: Minor: the RepairAgent 40 vs 22 iteration figure comes from Bouzenia and Pradel, the RepairAgent authors' own follow-up, so only the OpenHands 54 vs 25 rounds (Liu et al.) is truly independent support.

claim: LLM explanations of faults are mostly unreliable: about 20% accurate, 46.7% bland; scientific-debugging format with real execution gave 73% plausible vs 63% hallucinated execution. New (Kang et al.): AutoSD did not beat plain prompting on correct patches (Defects4J v1.2 76 vs 87; v2.0 113 vs 110; ARHE 187 vs 177 correct), so the gain is explanation and grounding, not accuracy.
agent_test: Compare hypothesis-experiment loop with real execution vs simulated execution.

claim: Fine-tuned small code models can localise without tests: UniXcoder 50.6% Top-1 of 1,291 methods; model size did not help; LLMAO unseen projects top-1 31.9%.
agent_test: Use a cheap fine-tuned ranker as a prior only if training allowed (we do not train); low priority.
audit_note: Minor: the LLMAO 31.9% unseen-project figure is for CodeGen-16B, which is not a small model; UniXcoder is 125M.

claim: Spectrum methods fail on coincidental correctness and missing-code faults; a passing test touching a line does not clear it.
agent_test: Do not treat passing-coverage as clearing a line in the agent's suspect ranking.

claim: Adding an Ochiai suspiciousness list to an LLM prompt gives a small gain and was not seen to harm: +3.7% Top-1 over chain-of-thought (169 vs 163 of 324 student faults, GPT-3.5); +0.4 to +4.3 points repair accuracy on 3,902 Codeflaws bugs across three Llama models. No equal-token test and no repository-scale agent test exists.
agent_test: Ablate the spectrum hint in the agent at equal tokens; report Top-1 and cost; include a degraded list arm.

claim: Defects4J shows signs of memorisation: 80% of its repositories are in TheStack and older or mid-size open models such as codegen-6B-multi reproduce it (82% 5-gram accuracy), and repair success on Defects4J falls significantly after meaning-preserving edits for all seven LLMs tested (from -4.0 points for GPT-4o to -16.0 for Llama-3.1), with larger drops for models that find the original bugs more familiar (low NLL); frontier models show smaller drops and less leakage signal, and these sources test full repair, not localisation alone.
agent_test: Evaluate on identifier-renamed and post-cutoff bugs; report both.
audit_note: Sources show leakage signals (80% TheStack membership, low NLL, 82% 5-gram for codegen-6B) and significant drops after transformation for all seven models (even Claude-3.7 -4.89 and GPT-4o -4.01), but neither proves Defects4J scores are 'inflated'; the 'localisation-only version has not been run' claim is a negative that neither source addresses.
claim_before_audit: Defects4J numbers are inflated by memorisation in older and mid-size open models, and repair success on it falls after meaning-preserving edits; frontier-model effect is smaller and a localisation-only version has not been run.

claim: Agents fail in two opposite ways after finding a fault: they stop without a valid test (premature termination, fixes written without testing) and they loop (repeated identical searches, long tails of 54 rounds vs 25 for successes). Overthinking scores correlate negatively with resolution (slopes -7.9 reasoning, -15.9 non-reasoning).
agent_test: Add a verify-once trigger, a repeat-action detector and a round cap near 25; log premature stops.
audit_note: Minor: 'two opposite ways' and 'after finding a fault' are the notes' framing; sources list the anti-patterns (repeated identical actions, fixes without testing, termination without test validation) and the 54 vs 25 rounds and -7.894/-15.938 slopes, which all match.

claim: Multi-file faults are the clearest class that defeats current tools: single-file success 55-58% against OpenHands 25.3% on multi-file issues (SWE-bench Verified); about 65% of failure root causes are flawed reasoning such as keyword fixation, and pipelines fail mostly at localisation while agents fail in iteration.
agent_test: After the first fix, enumerate coupled files and call sites explicitly; measure multi-file resolution.

claim: Resampling and re-planning are weakly separated: at equal cost, extra serial iterations and extra parallel samples give similar coverage after a few iterations; backtracking search gave a 23% relative gain but at larger compute; a supervisor agent resolved 22.2% of previously failed issues. A clean re-localise-versus-resample test at matched tokens is still missing.
agent_test: Compare re-localise-after-N-failures against N more samples at equal tokens.

claim: File-level localisation is largely solved by brute force: an LLM scanning every file kept the gold files in a 128k context for 92.6% of SWE-bench Verified issues at about 15% of cost; the open problem is symbol or line level and issue-quality dependence.
agent_test: Use cheap file-level scan, then spend tokens on symbol-level checks.
